correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge6\) and \(3\le k\le n-3\), the orbit-barycenter construction models exactly the geometric fixed points, not merely pointwise-fixed original vertices. The three orbit types have all pairwise clique-compatibilities checked explicitly, yielding two smaller Johnson clique complexes connected by \(\binom{n-2}{k-1}\) homotopy intervals. A self-contained clique-facet collapse leaves a simply connected 2-complex, whose integral Euler characteristic and Hurewicz–Whitehead argument prove the b(m,j) sphere wedge. The finite verifier constructs original vertex orbits and complete orbit simplices, independently computing exact mod-two boundary ranks for ten parameter pairs from (6,3) through (11,5), agreeing with every predicted Betti number and higher-dimensional vanishing. These finite tests are corroboration, not the proof of universality.

value.rationale: An infinite two-parameter classification of geometric transposition-fixed homotopy types of a standard Johnson/hypersimplex family determines integral \(\pi_1\) as a free group of rank \(\binom{n-2}{k-1}-1\), as well as all integral Betti numbers. The ambient complexes are simply connected sphere wedges, yet the fixed spaces have arbitrarily high-rank free \(\pi_1\); this genuine equivariant topological phenomenon is not inferable from ordinary Betti numbers, ordinary homotopy types, or rational ambient symmetry characters. It is structurally natural, not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine numerical improvement.
